title: Turn waste into
biochar that pays.
hero.lede: A self-powered rocket-stove pyrolysis system for fibrous crop waste. It turns fruit bunches, coir and husk into biochar, and its own gas keeps the fire going, so nothing goes to waste.

why.light_it_once_with_a: Light it once with a handful of dry waste. From then on the reactor keeps its own fire going, so there’s no diesel, gas or firewood to buy.
why.the_reactor_s_own_gas: The reactor’s own gas spins the fan that feeds the fire. No battery, no mains, no generator.
why.palm_mills_have_fruit_bunches: Palm mills have fruit bunches, rice mills have husk and coconut processors have coir. One reactor handles all three, and every batch gives you biochar plus usable ash.

parts.name: Reactor and lid
parts.body: A 254 L steel tube holds each batch. The lid bolts down tight, so the biomass chars without air instead of burning.

parts.name: Gauge and valve
parts.body: The gauge on the lid tells you how the pressure is building inside. Open the globe valve to send the gas down the pipe to the fan.

parts.name: Rocket stove
parts.body: An insulated stove under the reactor. Light it through the fuel door and slide out the ash drawer when the batch is done.

parts.name: Gas-driven fan
parts.body: Spun by the reactor’s own gas, it blows air back into the fire. No battery, no plug.

parts.name: Gas pipe
parts.body: Takes the hot gas from the reactor down to the fan. That’s what keeps the fan spinning.

parts.name: Frame and handle
parts.body: A steel A-frame carries the reactor. Turn the wheel to tip the tube and empty out the biochar.

steps.title: Load the reactor
steps.body: Fill the reactor tube with dry, chopped biomass. Close the lid and tighten the six bolts so no air can get in.

steps.title: Light the rocket stove
steps.body: Start the fire with a handful of dry waste, like fruit bunches, coir or husk, and a match. The rocket stove heats up fast, to between 450 and 660 °C.

steps.title: Spread the heat
steps.body: The stove has several burners, so flames run up the middle and around the sides and the whole batch cooks evenly. Insulation keeps the heat in and the outer wall safe to touch.

steps.title: Send the hot gas to the fan
steps.body: As the biomass heats up, it gives off hot gas under pressure. A pipe takes that gas from the reactor to the fan.

steps.title: The gas spins the fan
steps.body: The gas rushes through the fan and spins it. No electricity needed. The machine runs on what it makes.

steps.title: Steady the flame
steps.body: The fan blows air back into the fire, so the flame burns bigger and steadier.

steps.title: Unload the reactor
steps.body: When the batch is done, turn the wheel to tip the reactor on its side. Open the lid and take out the biochar.

steps.title: Biochar ready to use
steps.body: Your biochar comes out high in carbon and low in ash. Spread it on your fields or sell it to buyers.
